   shall be spent to benefit only the parcels or businesses in the prior district. If the renewed district does not
  include parcels or businesses included in the prior district, the remaining revenues attributable to these parcels
  shall be refunded to the owners of these parcels or businesses.
  (c) Upon renewal, a district shall have a term not to exceed 10 years, or, if the district is authorized to issue
  bonds, until the maximum maturity of those bonds. There is no requirement that the boundaries, assessments,
  improvements, or activities of a renewed district be the same as the original or prior district.

  CHAPTER 6. Disestablishment

36670. Circumstances permitting disestablishment of district; Procedure

  (a) Any district established or extended pursuant to the provisions of this part, where there is no indebtedness,
  outstanding and unpaid, incurred to accomplish any of the purposes of the district, may be disestablished by
  resolution by the city council in either of the following circumstances:
  (1) If the city council finds there has been misappropriation of funds, malfeasance, or a violation of
  law in connection with the management of the district, it shall notice a hearing on disestablishment.
  (2) During the operation of the district, there shall be a 30-day period each year in which assessees
  may request disestablishment of the district. The first such period shall begin one year after the date
  of establishment of the district and shall continue for 30 days. The next such 30-day period shall
  begin two years after the date of the establishment of the district. Each successive year of operation
  of the district shall have such a 30-day period. Upon the written petition of the owners or authorized
  representatives of real property or the owners or authorized representatives of businesses in the
  district who pay 50 percent or more of the assessments levied, the city council shall pass a resolution
  of intention to disestablish the district. The city council shall notice a hearing on disestablishment.
  (b) The city council shall adopt a resolution of intention to disestablish the district prior to the public hearing
  required by this section. The resolution shall state the reason for the disestablishment, shall state the time and
  place of the public hearing, and shall contain a proposal to dispose of any assets acquired with the revenues
  of the assessments levied within the property and business improvement district. The notice of the hearing
  on disestablishment required by this section shall be given by mail to the property owner of each parcel or to
  the owner of each business subject to assessment in the district, as appropriate. The city shall conduct the
  public hearing not less than 30 days after mailing the notice to the property or business owners. The public
  hearing shall be held not more than 60 days after the adoption of the resolution of intention.

36671. Refund of remaining revenues upon disestablishment or expiration without renewal of district;
Calculation of refund; Use of outstanding revenue collected after disestablishment of district

  (a) Upon the disestablishment or expiration without renewal of a district, any remaining revenues, after all
  outstanding debts are paid, derived from the levy of assessments, or derived from the sale of assets acquired
  with the revenues, or from bond reserve or construction funds, shall be refunded to the owners of the property
  or businesses then located and operating within the district in which assessments were levied by applying the
  same method and basis that was used to calculate the assessments levied in the fiscal year in which the district
  is disestablished or expires. All outstanding assessment revenue collected after disestablishment shall be
  spent on improvements and activities specified in the management district plan.
  (b) If the disestablishment occurs before an assessment is levied for the fiscal year, the method and basis that
  was used to calculate the assessments levied in the immediate prior fiscal year shall be used to calculate the
  amount of any refund.

Under the Purchase and Sale Agreement, Covington will purchase approximately 96
acres of vacant land located at the southeast corner of Avenue M and Sierra Highway
in, Palmdale, California, APN: 3126-022-929 (“Property”), with a first right to negotiate
the purchase of two additional, adjacent 86-acre parcels of vacant land from the City
if the initial 1,000,000 square feet of building space is completed based on the
schedule of performance outlined in the Purchase and Sales Agreement A-7575. At
Covington’s sole cost, they will pursue the obtainment of any required environmental
clearance, zoning, platting, replatting, site plan, utility, parcel splits, and other
entitlements, development approvals and permits from the applicable governmental
authorities and from utility companies as necessary for the 96 acres in Phase I to be
in "shovel ready" condition for Covington's intended development.

Under Assembly Bill (AB)1486, Surplus Land Act (SLA) local agencies are required to
notice the disposal of surplus land. Therefore, in order to sell this Property, the City
was required to declare this Property “surplus land” at a public meeting before taking
any action to dispose of it. On April 6, 2021, City Council adopted Resolution CC
2021-023 declaring parcels APN 3126-022-926, APN 3126-022-927, APN 3126-022-
928, and APN 3126-022-929 as surplus property. The City sent out a written notice of
availability (NOA) to the Housing Sponsors list and other local public entities identified
by the California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) on April
7, 2021. These entities had 60 days from April 7, 2021, to submit a notice of intent to
negotiate purchase or lease of the property. The City did not receive any notices of
interest within the 60-day time period in accordance with the guidelines of the SLA
(Government Code Section 54220-54234).

DISCUSSION
Agreement No. A-7575 constitutes a purchase and sale agreement by which the City
agrees to sell to Covington and Covington agrees to purchase the property and to
construct, or cause to be constructed, a minimum 1,000,000 square feet of new
Industrial, Aerospace Industrial and Employment Flex building(s) aimed to protect,
support, and expand operations at U.S. Air Force Plant 42 and to create new
employment opportunities for residents. This may include new buildings constructed
for either sale or lease or through the direct sale of entitled parcels to businesses
seeking to construct a new facility. Covington will work with the City and external
agencies to obtain all entitlements needed for the construction and development of the
Property. Covington will also work closely with Edwards Air Force Base and the U.S.
Air Force Plant 42 to ensure this project will not negatively impact the Air Force or the
contractors at U.S. Air Force Plant 42. The City estimates that over 800 permanent

full-time jobs and thousands of temporary construction jobs will be created from the
onsite and offsite development associated with the Property.

As part of the entitlement process, Covington shall prepare a Specific Plan that shall
address standards and restrictions regarding the construction and development of the
Project including, but not limited to, maximum land coverage, setbacks, land use
standards, architectural standards, building height, parking, and landscaping.

The Covington Project will not impact the development of the proposed solar land
lease project or future airport project. Offsite improvements like the installation of new
streets, will be built to accommodate all proposed projects in this area. Additionally,
Covington shall construct and install all public improvements and utilities required by
the City, and other approving agencies, and all other public improvements and utilities
necessary for the Project.

If the initial 1,000,000 square feet of building space is completed based on the schedule
of performance outlined in the Purchase and Sales Agreement No. A-7575, Covington
will have the opportunity to negotiate the purchase of additional City owned land
located adjacent to the Property.

FISCAL IMPACT
The sale price is $2.25 per square foot or $9,408,960 based on 96 acres. City and
Covington agree to adjust the purchase price prior to Close of Escrow in the event
and to the extent the Property is determined to be larger or smaller in size by a survey
approved by City and Covington.

The following Summary Report has been prepared pursuant to California Government Code
Sections 52200 - 52201. The report sets forth certain details of the proposed Purchase and
Sale Agreement (PSA) to convey 96 acres of City-owned property located on the southeast
corner of Avenue M and Sierra Highway (Property). The PSA is proposed between the City of
Palmdale (City) and Covington Investments, LLC (Purchaser), a Nevada limited liability
company.

AGREEMENT OVERVIEW

The following summary is based upon the information contained within the PSA to address
the items outlined in California Government Code Sections 52201(B):

I.  COST OF THE AGREEMENT TO THE CITY

  The City of Palmdale acquired 616 total acres of vacant land at the southeast corner of
  Avenue M and Sierra Highway for $18,000,000.00 or $0.67 per square foot. The PSA
  includes the sale of 96 acres of the total approximately 616-acre site. Based on the per
  square foot price, the cost to the City for the 96 acres being sold would be
  $2,801,779.20.

  As a result of the disposition of the Property, the City incurred limited costs associated
  with the negotiation and preparation of the PSA and other costs related to due diligence
  activities. The City also anticipates standard costs associated with the property
  transaction that will be determined upon close of escrow. There are no other financial
  obligations included in the PSA

II.  ESTIMATED VALUE OF THE INTEREST TO BE CONVEYED DETERMINED AT THE
  HIGHEST USE PERMITTED UNDER THE GENERAL PLAN OR ZONING

  An appraisal for the 96-acre site that is included in the PSA was done by Mission Property
  Advisors, Inc. on August 6, 2021. The estimated value of the Property was Five Million
  Nine hundred and Sixty-Five Thousand dollars ($5,965,000.00). The appraisal took into
  consideration the current zoning and the types of development allowed under the zone
  designation.

III.  ESTIMATED VALUE OF THE INTEREST TO BE CONVEYED DETERMINED AT THE
  USE WITH THE CONDITIONS, COVENANTS, AND DEVELOPMENT COSTS
  REQUIRED BY THE SALE

  As outlined in the PSA, the Purchaser shall construct, or cause to be constructed, a
  minimum one million square feet of new industrial or employment flex building(s) on the
  Property. The price that the City is receiving for the property is Nine Million Four hundred
 Page 2

City of Palmdale and Covington Investments, LLC

  and Eight Thousand Nine Hundred and Sixty Dollars ($9,408,960.00). The purchase price
  has been calculated based on per square foot price of Two Dollars and Twenty-Five Cents
  ($2.25) and the Property being ninety-six (96) acres in size. The City and Purchaser agree
  to adjust the purchase price prior to close of escrow in the event and to the extent the
  Property is determined to be larger or smaller in size by a survey approved by the City and
  Purchaser.

  Based on the sale price and estimated value of the Property, the City is not selling below
  the fair market value as estimated by an independent appraiser.

IV.  CREATION OF ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY

  Palmdale, and the greater Antelope Valley, has experienced low industrial vacancy rates
  over the past few years. Most recently during the second quarter of 2021, the industrial
  vacancy rate for the Antelope Valley was 3.4%. The lack of available industrial space,
  coupled with the lack of shovel-ready sites available for development, has impacted the
  City’s ability to attract new business and assist existing businesses looking to expand.
  Most businesses seeking new sites are not willing to wait the twelve months or more
  needed to get a potential site entitled for development.

  Under the PSA, a minimum one million square feet of new industrial or employment flex
  space will be constructed on the Property. This may include new buildings constructed
  for either sale or lease or through the direct sale of entitled parcels to businesses seeking
  to construct a new facility. The Purchaser will work with the City and external agencies to
  obtain all entitlements needed for the construction and development of the Property. The
  City estimates that over 800 permanent full-time jobs and thousands of temporary
  construction jobs will be created from the onsite and offsite development associated with
  the Property.

  If the initial one million square feet of building space is completed based on the schedule
  of performance outlined in the PSA, the Purchaser will have the opportunity to negotiate
  the purchase of additional City owned land located adjacent to the Property.

ISSUE
Adopt Ordinance No. 1570 Amending the Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.04.100
regarding procedure for removal of the City Manager.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Ordinance No. 1570 regarding the
procedure for removal of the City Manager.

BACKGROUND
On February 18, 2021, the City Council directed the City Attorney’s Office to prepare an
Ordinance amending Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 2.04.100 regarding the
procedure for the removal of the City Manager. This direction came on the City Council
agreeing to amend an agreement with the City Manager that he not be removed absent
a four-fifths, supermajority, vote of the City Council.

On September 7, 2021, the City Council directed the City Attorney’s Office to work with
the City Manager to return with an Ordinance that reverts to the simple-majority, three-
fifths removal provision, but with ample protections relating to the current City Manager’s
employment agreement. That Ordinance is presented for consideration herein.

DISCUSSION
The proposed amendment to Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.04.100 is as follows
(marked in red and strikethrough):
PMC 2.04.100 Removal – Procedure.

(A) The removal of the City Manager shall be only on a super majority, four-fifths vote of
the whole City Council, subject, however, to the provisions of PMC 2.04.110, and subject
to any additional requirements for removal of the City Manager, including additional super
 Report to Mayor and City Council

Page 2

majority requirements as contractually obligated to a City Manager by the City Council.
Any change made to this provision shall not take effect until the expiration of the then
existing agreement with the City Manager. In case of intended removal by the City
Council, the City Manager shall be furnished with a written notice stating that the City
Council’s intention is to remove the City Manager and the reasons therefor at least 30
days before the effective date of any such removal.

(B) Within seven days after delivery to the City Manager of such notice, the City Manager
may, by written notification to the Mayor, request a public hearing before the City Council.
Thereafter, the City Council shall fix a time for a public hearing, which shall be held at its
usual meeting place, but before the expiration of the 30-day period, and at which time the
City Manager shall have the opportunity to appear and be heard.

(C) After furnishing the City Manager with written notice of intended removal, the City
Council may suspend the City Manager from duty, but compensation shall continue until
removal of the City Manager by resolution of the City Council adopted subsequent to the
aforesaid public hearing.

(D) In removing the City Manager, the City Council shall have absolute discretion, and its
action shall be final and shall not depend upon any particular showing or degree of proof
at the hearing. The purpose of the hearing is to allow the City Manager to publicly present
to the City Council any and all grounds for opposition to removal prior to its action.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.
